title: Agfa Isolette: A Working Eye
summary: A compact body of square medium-format photographs uses a 1961 folding camera to study coastal structure, material, atmosphere, and the workshop.
searchSummary: Six photographs from a 12-image Agfa Isolette album, moving from Bolivar Peninsula and Galveston Bay to an intentional double exposure and a Lockerbie kickwheel.
stage: Twelve-photo album curated into a six-image sequence
sourceLabel: Agfa Isolette journal and Flickr album

gallery.caption: North Jetty Bait Camp opens the sequence with a vernacular structure held against the coastal atmosphere.
Galveston East Bay lets horizon and water settle into the square frame.
The jetty leads the eye through the frame and gives the Port Bolivar scene its depth.
Foreground rocks and distant ships test the detail held by the camera and scan path.
An intentional double exposure layers two views of Port Bolivar into one frame.
The Lockerbie Model K closes the sequence by bringing the camera from the coast back into the workshop.

introduction: The Agfa Isolette is old enough to require a slower kind of attention. Its square 120-film frame rewards clear structure, patient looking, and subjects with enough material presence to hold the image together.
evidenceBoundary: This is a six-image editorial selection from a 12-photo album. The double exposure is intentional, and the film camera is a 1961 Agfa Isolette.
